title: TSAcc: An Efficient Tempo-Spatial Similarity Aware Accelerator for Attention Acceleration
problem: Attention-based models in NLP and CV have heavy computational and memory demands. Previous work optimizes only within sentences, missing acceleration opportunities across successive sentences.
motivation: Accelerating attention mechanisms is critical for practical deployment of large transformer models that dominate NLP and computer vision applications.
method: TSAcc exploits the observation that successive sentences have high token/head similarity. It uses an online-offline prediction algorithm to identify similar tokens and heads, then applies a recovery algorithm that skips computation on similar elements in subsequent sentences by copying results from preceding sentences. A specialized hardware architecture implements prediction and recovery engines to realize these computational savings in practice.
key_novelty: Leveraging temporal similarity across successive sentences to skip redundant attention computations, in contrast to prior work that only optimizes within single sentences.
contributions: Observation that successive sentences exhibit high similarity in attention patterns due to semantic overlap in tokens
Online-offline prediction algorithm to identify similar tokens and attention heads across temporal boundaries
Recovery algorithm enabling result reuse by copying features from preceding to subsequent sentences
Specialized TSAcc hardware architecture with integrated prediction and recovery engines

metrics.speedup: 8.5X vs SpAtten, 2.7X vs Sanger, 14.1X vs 1080TI GPU, 64.9X vs Xeon CPU

primary_theme: Temporal similarity exploitation for attention acceleration
